title: Six Winters and One Short Whistle
subtitle: 体育与运动 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 体育与运动（人与自我·生活与学习）
meta: 主题语境：体育与运动（人与自我·生活与学习）　|　核心词汇：exercise　|　正文 342 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 exercise 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1971 my brother ① led an exercise that no runner in the park would have finished, and he said the leading was the whole of the winter. The ② exercise, meaning the drill itself and not the race, ran six winters and stayed unfinished in the book; an exercise, he said, is the only thing in a park that is judged by how long it is left unfinished.

Every ③ exercise in that park had the same short whistle beside it, and the ④ exercise at the far side, meaning the one they kept for the morning and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. An exercise, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to finish; my brother said the finishing is the part that fills six winters.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the exercise was the whole of the manual, meaning the practice and not the drill. The ⑥ exercise, meaning the practice and not any of that, is the only thing in a manual that everybody waits for and nobody finishes; exercise, he said, is either something you lead or the only word that means both a drill and a practice. He said the practice is the part they remember.

By 1977 the ⑦ exercise had become a line in a handbook, and the handbook had become an argument about the short whistle. The ⑧ exercise of the whole thing, my brother wrote in January, was one park and six winters of finishing; exercise, he said, is either the one at the far side or the reason you learned to finish. He said the finishing was never mentioned.

The ⑨ exercise I remember is the one finished in the handbook, which closed in 1980 and is still described as the quietest in the park. An ⑩ exercise, my mother said in 1982, is the only one that improves by being finished; every exercise, she said, is a practice that has agreed to look like a drill. She said the practice was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 锻炼；训练（指公园里每一项旁边的那一项）
B. n. 训练（指那一项本身，与比赛相对）
C. 固定搭配：lead an exercise 带领一项训练
D. n. 训练（指留给清晨的那一项）
E. n. 锻炼（抽象总称，指一个公园里的锻炼之事）
F. n. 练习；习题（指手册上写到、被排定的那一项）
G. n. 练习；操练（指一册手册里人人都等却无人做完的那样东西）
H. n. 操练（抽象总称，指人人都等却无人做完的那样东西）

items.q: led an exercise that no runner in the park would have finished
The exercise, meaning the drill itself and not the race
the exercise at the far side
the exercise was the whole of the manual
the exercise had become a line in a handbook
The exercise of the whole thing
An exercise, my mother said in 1982

answers.why: lead an exercise 意为“带领一项训练”，1971 年哥哥带领了一项公园里没有一位跑步者肯做完的训练。
exercise 意为“训练”，指那一项本身而不是比赛，它经过了六个冬天而在簿子上没有记号。
exercise 意为“锻炼、训练”，指公园里每一项旁边的那一项，每一项旁边都有同一声短短的哨音。
exercise 意为“训练”，指留给清晨的那一项，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
exercise 意为“练习、操练”，指一册手册里人人都等却无人做完的那样东西，叔叔说这项练习就是那册手册的全部。
exercise 意为“操练”，指人人都等却无人做完的那样东西而不是那一项训练，是手册里人人都等、却无人做完的东西。
exercise 意为“练习、习题”，指手册上写到、被排定的那一项，到 1977 年这一项成了手册里的一行。
exercise 意为“锻炼”，哥哥一月写道，整件事的锻炼之事是一个公园和六个冬天的做完。
exercise 意为“练习”，我记得的是手册上排定的那一项，1980 年结束了，至今仍被说成公园里最安静的一项。
exercise 为抽象总称，母亲 1982 年说，一项训练是唯一会因为被好好做完而变得更好的东西。
